Articles

Start here

A short path for each kind of user.

Start here: Students

A path for graduate students: Fit, check and explain an IRT model for a course or thesis, with figures a committee will accept.

Start here: Instructors

A complete IRT course in a box: A free book, ten interactive labs, a course map, and tools to adapt everything to your own data.

Start here: Testing programs

For psychometricians at testing organizations and credentialing bodies: Run a program from blueprint to bank monitoring, with every decision flagged, reviewed and documented.

Start here: Researchers

All of mirt, with tidy outputs, ggplot2 figures and one-call reports, so analyses are reproducible and figures are publication-ready.

Start here: New to R

Get IRT results without learning R first: Point and click in the workbench, describe the analysis in words, or share a dashboard.

mirtverse paketinin Türkçe tanıtımı: Paketin ne yaptığı, kurulumu, ilk analiz ve Türkçe özet kılavuz.

Guides

Tutorial: A first analysis with mirtverse
The mirtverse workbench
Which IRT model? A one-page flowchart

A decision flowchart that goes from what one item score looks like to an IRT model and the line of R code that fits it, with a printable poster and a worked example for every path.

Response times and rapid guessing
mv_ask(): From a sentence to a tested R script

How mv_ask() turns a plain-language request into a complete IRT analysis script, with worked examples and benchmark results for Claude, GPT and local Ollama models.

The mirtverse agent for Claude

Install the mirtverse plugin for Claude Code and let Claude analyze your test data with item response theory: Model choice, item checks, DIF, scores, plots, a report and a reproducible R script.

Sharing results with a dashboard

Turn a fitted model into an interactive dashboard for people who do not use R, and share it as a single HTML file or a Shiny app.

Moving from ltm, eRm, TAM or irtQ to mirt

Translate existing IRT code into mirt with mirtify(), see what changes and why, and look up any function in the crosswalk.

An assessment pipeline from blueprint to bank monitoring

Take a certification exam through every stage of the mirtverse assessment pipeline, with the checks and decisions at each step.

Case study: A certification exam, from field test to pass/fail

A fictional certification board takes a 32-item exam through the mirtverse assessment pipeline. Eight decisions, each recorded, and a technical report to download.

Thesis kit: From item responses to a Methods section

A step-by-step path for a thesis or dissertation that uses IRT: Check the data, choose and check a model, make the figures, and draft the Methods paragraph with cite_methods().

Gallery

Every figure and output mirtverse makes, with the code for each one.

Video demos

Short narrated demos of mirtverse: The point-and-click workbench, the AI Hub and the thesis kit, about 90 seconds each with English captions.

Teaching and learning

Adopt mirtverse for your course

Everything an instructor needs to teach item response theory with mirtverse: A sample syllabus to edit, a free book, ten labs, and a way to hear about updates.

Teaching labs for measurement courses

Interactive learnr labs in which students fit live mirt models and make the decisions a psychometrician makes, from scoring and model choice to interpretation and fairness. Includes an instructor guide and answer key.

A course map for instructors

A suggested 12-week syllabus for a university course in item response theory, linking each week to mirtverse articles, labs, functions and datasets.

The instructor toolkit

Build interactive labs on your own data, adapt the built-in labs and the book’s chapters, add exercises and questions, swap datasets, and check everything before class.

An AI assistant for your course materials

Connect Claude or an OpenAI assistant to your mirtverse course folder and revise labs, chapters and notes, or bring your existing materials into mirtverse, by describing what you want.

Glossary of IRT terms

Plain-language definitions of the terms used in item response theory, each with the mirtverse or mirt function that computes it, and pictures where a picture helps.

AI in measurement

Artificial intelligence and machine learning for psychometricians. These articles are also in the AI Hub menu.

AI Hub: Artificial intelligence for psychometricians

Start here to learn how artificial intelligence and machine learning fit into psychometrics and educational measurement: A learning path, what mirtverse can already do with AI, and where to read more.

Checking synthetic respondents: The coverage strip

How to see where respondents generated by a language model land in the real population, how to read Overlap and Structure, and how to compare models, groups and items, with HEXACO answers from four language models and 17,874 real people.

Machine learning for psychometricians: A translation table

More than 40 machine learning and AI terms, each with what it means, the psychometric idea closest to it, and where the two part ways.

AI in measurement: A reading list

An annotated list of books, papers and guidelines on artificial intelligence in psychometrics and educational measurement, grouped by topic, for psychometricians who are new to the area.

AI in measurement: A one-day workshop

A ready-made kit for a one-day workshop on AI in measurement: Slides, a facilitator’s guide and four offline labs, for psychometricians and testing-program staff.
